advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _carries_store_structure treat a non-transient OSError from published_is_file as 'no record' (or convert it to the store_uninitialized path) instead of letting it escape store_is_usable
evidence: src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:105-108: try: return stat.S_ISREG(retry_contended(os.stat, path).st_mode) except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError): return False
Removed line: `if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, COMPAT_FILENAME)):` — os.path.exists returns False on any OSError
src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py:59-62: the next probe still degrades with `except OSError: return False`, so the module's convention is a probe that never raises
src/rebar/_reads.py:56-64: callers expect a bool and turn False into a RebarError with error_code 'store_uninitialized'
advisory.finding: _carries_store_structure switched from os.path.exists (never raises) to published_is_file, which only maps FileNotFoundError/NotADirectoryError to False. Any other OSError from the stat (e.g. EACCES on a tracker dir without search permission, or ELOOP) now escapes store_is_usable as a raw exception. It used to return False and fall through to the listdir/git checks, so library reads now surface an unclassified OSError instead of the structured 'store_uninitialized' RebarError.
scenarios: POSIX tracker directory that is readable but not searchable: the stat of .store-compat.json raises PermissionError, which now propagates out of every read through _reads.py instead of returning a classified error
Windows host with a genuinely access-denied compat file: the probe now spins 2s and then raises
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the call: `try: if published_is_file(...): return True\nexcept OSError: pass` so that only the retry behaviour changes and the probe still never raises.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle the Windows directory-open PermissionError in load_eval_spec (and the other removed is_file sites), e.g. re-check os.path.isdir after a PermissionError before retrying or falling back
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:85-86: except OSError as exc: raise EvalError(...)
src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:73-77: except PermissionError: if time.monotonic() >= deadline: raise ... time.sleep(sleep_s)
Removed line: `if not path.is_file(): path = _packaged_eval_spec(prompt_id)` — a directory used to route to the packaged spec on every platform
The same pre-check removal applies in prompts.py get_prompt/_prompt_file, checkpoints.load_checkpoint and scratch._get: on Windows a directory at the path now costs a 2s stall before degrading
advisory.finding: Windows reports opening a directory as PermissionError (errno 13), not IsADirectoryError. With the is_file() pre-checks removed, open_published on a path that is a directory spins in retry_contended until the 2s deadline and then raises PermissionError. In load_eval_spec this also skips the packaged-spec fallback the inner except was written for (it catches only FileNotFoundError/IsADirectoryError/NotADirectoryError), so the code raises EvalError where it used to fall back.
scenarios: On Windows, a directory exists at .rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml (or .rebar/prompts/<id>.md): the read stalls 2s, and the eval loader raises instead of using the built-in spec

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the AST call-name census with behavioral tests that call each reader under a forced Windows-branch refusal and check the value it returns
evidence: assert function in found, f"{module}: no function {function}; update this list"
assert called & _HELPERS, f"{module}:{function} reads a published file without a retry"
_READERS maps 28 production source paths (e.g. "src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py": ("byte_total",)) to function names, so the test pins implementation text rather than observable output
advisory.finding: test_each_exposed_reader_uses_a_retried_read greps the source under test with ast. For each of 28 readers it checks that the function body calls a name in {open_published, published_is_file, retry_contended} and no name in {exists, is_file, isfile}. This is a change-detector: a behavior-preserving refactor breaks it. Examples are renaming a reader, or moving its open into a private helper (the case asserts `function in found` and only looks at direct calls in that function's body). It is also regression-blind: a reader can call open_published on one path and still swallow a refusal and return a default on another, and every case stays green.
scenarios: Extracting the open in binding_repository._load into a shared `_open_store()` helper fails the case even though behavior is unchanged
Renaming session_log._read_pointer fails the case even though behavior is unchanged
A reader that calls open_published but wraps it in `except PermissionError: return default` still passes
advisory.suggested_fix: Delete the AST test, or keep it only as an advisory lint. For each reader (or at least the fail-open and fail-closed representatives), add a test that uses the existing windows_branch fixture, monkeypatches builtins.open (or os.stat for published_is_file callers) with _refuse_then(..., refusals=1), and checks the reader's real return value. For example, write '123' to the byte-total file and check that byte_total(root) == 123.

Commit message: 'readers that fail open took a wrong default that can be written back (a new session log replacing its pointer, bridge repair's retired-key guard, a doubled snapshot byte total, a gate run record read as absent)'
advisory.finding: No test drives a changed reader through a transient refusal, so the harmful outcomes named in the commit message have no regression test. Several readers drop their existence check and now decide absence from FileNotFoundError: binding_repository._load/_load_retired/retired_entries, projects_store.load_mapping, bridge_fsck._read_integrity_store, bridge_repair._retired_keys and _cli._suggest_mapping_write. None of these paths is exercised under the forced Windows branch, and _suggest_mapping_write has no test reference except the AST list. A concrete input: with windows_branch active and builtins.open refusing once, BindingRepository._load on an existing bindings.json must return the parsed store, not raise ValueError(_corrupt_live_message). The same applies to session_log._read_pointer on an existing pointer, which must return the pointer and not None. Nothing tests either.
scenarios: Someone later adds a pre-read check, or catches PermissionError inside a reader, and the fail-open default comes back with no test failing
